subject.title: Gateway should log warning when message is dropped due to allow: false

question: Should allow:false policy-denial warnings be implemented first as a Slack-owned ingress diagnostic, or as a shared channel ingress diagnostic contract across channels?
rationale: Both shapes are plausible: the source-reproducible incident is Slack-specific, but the issue asks for gateway/channel-level structured diagnostics and dedupe, which can become a shared contract if maintainers want cross-channel consistency.

options.title: Slack-owned warning first
options.body: Add a focused Slack warning for explicit channel denial with account/channel/reason fields and local dedupe, then generalize only after another channel needs it.

options.title: Shared channel diagnostic seam
options.body: Define a common channel ingress denial logger around the message-access decision graph and route Slack through it, accepting a broader implementation surface now.

options.title: Keep verbose-only for now
options.body: Leave fail-closed channel drops as verbose diagnostics until maintainers decide logging volume and redaction policy are worth the warning-level noise.

recommendation.title: Slack-owned warning first
recommendation.body: Add a focused Slack warning for explicit channel denial with account/channel/reason fields and local dedupe, then generalize only after another channel needs it.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent PR and commit history shows the most current ownership signal around channel/gateway-adjacent runtime paths and Slack context maintenance.
